messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
At 10 kPa (≈0.1 bar) the melting/freezing point of water is essentially the same as at atmospheric pressure.  
Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the ice–water transition, the slope of the melting curve near the triple point is only about –2 × 10⁻⁴ K kPa⁻¹. Over the 3.9 kPa difference between 10 kPa and the triple‑point pressure (6.112 kPa) the temperature shift is less than 0.001 K.  

**Result**

| Pressure | Freezing point (°C) |
|----------|---------------------|
| 10 kPa   | ≈ 0.00 °C (273.15 K) |

So, at 10 kPa water freezes at roughly 0 °C, with a negligible deviation (on the order of a few millikelvin).
